claims.finding: Lands' End's own FY26 guidance, issued at the 2026-06-09 print, is net revenue of $1.30-1.40bn, adjusted EBITDA of $68-78m and NET INCOME of $310-320m - the last figure being roughly the entire market value of the equity at $11.27 - because the WHP Global transaction monetised the Lands' End intellectual property, and the company simultaneously has a $100m share repurchase agreement in place, about 29% of the market capitalisation.
claims.corpus_ref: docs/4b236ec1977fb78cc0d372d18adc6bc447a8957b.txt (snapshots/20260830T084126Z.json item 1), entries dated 2026-06-09T11:11:55Z and 2026-06-08T12:51:04Z; 8-K items '2.02,7.01,9.01' dated 2026-06-09 in filings.json
claims.why_not_priced: The guide is wire copy; the arithmetic is not, and nothing in the 88-item capture states it. The tape says the market is treating this as a shrinking cataloguer - revenue -8.5% YoY on distribution disruption - and has taken the stock down 11.9% over twenty sessions and 41% from its high, while the company is sitting on realised IP proceeds and an authorisation to retire nearly a third of the float. The buyback's execution pace is exactly what a quarterly release updates, and there is no news-search coverage of this ticker at all (n_queries=0 in every admissible sweep) to test it.
claims.independence: Noble Capital Markets initiated coverage on 2026-06-18 with precisely this thesis from an independent source - 'the transformational WHP Global partnership unlocks hidden brand value by monetizing the Lands' End intellectual property portfolio, eliminating significant balance-sheet risk... in our view, the market is underappreciating the long-term earnings potential' - https://www.channelchek.com/news-channel/lands-end-le-multiple-paths-to-value-creation

claims.finding: The last print behaved exactly the way a buyback-supported stock behaves: it opened down 5.8% pre-market on a revenue miss ('faces narrower loss but revenue miss on distribution disruption') and closed the session up 8.47% - a 14-point intraday reversal on 2026-06-09.
claims.corpus_ref: docs/4b236ec1977fb78cc0d372d18adc6bc447a8957b.txt entry dated 2026-06-09T12:29:17Z (-5.8% pre-market) against the baseline's recorded +8.47% reaction for 2026-06-09
claims.why_not_priced: The reversal is only visible by cross-referencing a pre-market quote in a Stocktwits post against the baseline's close-to-close reaction, which is exactly the kind of two-source join nothing publishes. It says the marginal buyer at this price is not reacting to the revenue line. It is the same event as finding 1's mechanism, so treat them as one cluster.
claims.independence: none - shares the same captured document and the same underlying release as finding 1.

claims.finding: A management-transition cluster sits in July: 8-Ks with item 5.02 on 2026-06-30 and again on 2026-07-10, an S-8 registration on 2026-07-14, a Form 3 and a Form 4 on 2026-07-15, and a Form 144 on 2026-07-23 - two officer or director changes eleven days apart followed immediately by a new-insider equity registration.
claims.why_not_priced: No body is stored and the Stocktwits stream never mentions any of it - the thread goes quiet after 2026-08-05. Two 5.02 filings inside a fortnight at a company mid-restructuring is a governance fact with no publisher, and it is the main thing that could make the guide unreliable, which is why I sign it against my other findings.
